facts.fact: Commentator Martin Čaban in Seznam Zprávy noted that the Labour Code amendment (sněmovní tisk 300) amends 22 existing laws and includes a controversial redefinition of dependent work alongside changes to unemployment benefits.

According to the official bill history on psp.cz, the Social Policy Committee issued its record of proceedings on print 300 on 12 November 2026, making the bill eligible for further debate from 20 November 2026 and placing its second reading on the proposed agenda of the 37th session starting 24 November 2026.
The Chamber of Deputies announced that the 37th session opens on Tuesday 24 November 2026 at 14:00 and includes on its proposed agenda the second and third readings of the 2027 state budget bill.

Trade union OSSOO reported that the ČMKOS union confederation launched a letter campaign to deputies opposing the second reading of the Labour Code amendment over its redefinition of dependent work and reduction of unemployment benefits.

Because ANO and Motorists hold 93 of 200 seats and lack a majority without SPD, Labour Minister Aleš Juchelka (ANO) prepared an amendment to soften the proposed unemployment benefit cuts, which the coalition council was set to confirm on Tuesday 24 November 2026.

Peníze.cz reported that under the coalition compromise amendment to the Labour Code bill, jobseekers aged 52 and older, those in retraining, and caregivers without prior calculated income will retain higher unemployment support rather than facing the cut from 80% to 65%.

Here the coalition majority, an announced compromise, and an authorised night sitting pull toward opening the reading on Thursday.
